samir_ml: Quick heads-up: peregrine-v2q (int4) streaming canary is spuriously returning concatenated NDJSON fragments for funcalls. Parser expects a single JSON object but we occasionally get two objects merged or a truncated second object. ~1.6% failure on 10k sample.

natalie: yikes. do you have a sanitized example? sounds like stream boundary vs batching reframe.

samir_ml: pasted two examples from the failing bucket. both reproduced locally with continuous-streaming + kv-prefix enabled:

```
Example A (glued complete objects):
{"req":"x1","tool":{"name":"summarize","args":{"text":"..."}}}
{"req":"x1","tool":{"name":"tag","args":{"labels":["a","b"]}}}

Example B (truncated suffix):
{"req":"x2","tool":{"name":"format","args":{"fields":["title","body"]}}}
{"req":"x2","tool":{"name":"format","args":{"fields":["title","body"]}  <-- missing closing braces / cut at token boundary
```

pavel: that truncated one smells like a tokenization/packing cut when the KV cache prefix gets merged into the stream. Did you try --disable-streaming or disable kv-cache?

samir_ml: yes. disable-streaming drops failures to 0.05%. disable-kvcache drops to 0.2%. so streaming+kvcache together is the likely interaction.

robin: quick mitigation: add a streaming sentinel in postprocess for canary (e.g., ensure each object ends with "\n" and a terminator token like "<END_JSON>" before parser). low-risk behind flag. Also consider NDJSON strict mode that rejects multiple objects rather than silently joining.

natalie: agree on sentinel. but we should root-cause: is kernel/quant packing chopping tokens or is the runtime streaming concat step dropping separator bytes? Instrumentation plan?

samir_ml: plan proposed:
1) instrument the runtime to capture raw token IDs and boundary indices for failing calls (last 48 tokens).
2) log KV-prefix snapshot length & content-hash per invoke.
3) run a micro-batch canary with runtime.kernel_fallback=true (safer kernel path) and compare failure delta.
4) add postprocess sentinel healer for immediate customer protection.

qa-bot: CI canary report 2025-03-11: peregrine-v2q int4 streaming ON, kvcache ON 🇳 pass 98.4% fail 1.6% (n=10000). Streaming OFF -> 99.95% pass. kvcache OFF -> 99.8% pass.

pavel: i'll take the kernel bisect if the token logs show truncated token IDs. robin, can you sketch the sentinel-healer patch? keep it toggleable.

robin: I'll open a tiny PR that wraps the stream parser: if parse error & streaming mode, try heuristics in order: 1) append closing braces until parse succeeds (max 4 chars), 2) strip non-printable control chars, 3) if NDJSON with multiple objects, split on newline and take first valid object. All behind FEATURE_NDJSON_HEALER. Add metrics for healed_vs_failed.

natalie: also check tokenizer config: tokenizer.escape_unmappable=false has caused similar missing-delimiter bugs in older kernels. try flip to true in instrumented run.

infra-bot: runtime release note: runtime-1.8.2 includes streaming concat sanity checks and an opt-in flag runtime.streaming_ndjson_sanitizer. Can be toggled per canary.

samir_ml: thanks. executing instrumented run now (50k samples) with kernel_fallback=true, tokenizer.escape_unmappable=true, feature flag enabled for healer. will post the CI summary + a small set of failing raw token dumps for pavel to bisect.

pavel: sounds good. if logs implicate quant packing we may need a patch in the int4 packing routine (pack_bits) to ensure we never split multi-byte token encodings across output flushes.

samir_ml: noted. will collect and upload to the canary bucket. ping here when done.
